question_text: A kind of bacteria grows as t³ (t in seconds). At what time is the rate of growth of the bacteria 300 bacteria per second?

mark_split.label: Differentiate and set the rate to 300

recall_prompt: Say how you would do this one — say which way round this question runs, and what you do with the 300.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Differentiate and set the rate to 300
steps.margin_note: First mark. This is a rate of growth question, but it runs the opposite way to the usual one: the rate is given and the time is asked. So the derivative goes on the left of an equals sign instead of being evaluated.
steps.memory_tip: Given the rate, asked the time: differentiate first, then write an equation, then solve.
lines: This is a rate of growth question. Here the rate is given and the time is asked,
so the derivative is set equal to the given rate.
Let N = t³ be the number of bacteria at time t seconds.

recall.must_convey: That dN/dt = 3t² and that this derivative is set equal to 300.
accept: differentiate t cubed to get three t squared and set it equal to three hundred
the rate is given so equate the derivative to three hundred
here we are given the rate and asked the time
derivative ni three hundred ki equal cheyyali
three t squared equals three hundred

steps.why: Every other question in this group substitutes a time and reads off a rate. This one gives the rate, so the derivative is equated to 300 and the equation is solved for t.
common_mistakes: Setting t³ = 300, which answers a different question.

steps.label: Solve for t
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Write t = ±10 and then say in words why −10 is rejected — an examiner looks for the rejection, not only the 10.
steps.memory_tip: Two roots, one clock: time is measured forward from zero, so a negative root is not a time.
lines: Time cannot be negative, so t = −10 is rejected.

lines.text: ∴ the rate of growth is 300 bacteria per second at t = 10 sec

recall.must_convey: That t² = 100 gives t = ±10 and that only t = 10 seconds is accepted.
accept: t squared is one hundred so t is plus or minus ten
time cannot be negative so t is ten seconds
reject minus ten because time is never negative
minus ten reject cheyyali, t equals ten seconds

steps.why: t² = 100 has two roots, but t is a time measured from the start of the growth, so only the positive root is a possible answer.
common_mistakes: Giving t = ±10 as the final answer without rejecting the negative root.
Taking the square root of 300 instead of dividing by 3 first.

insider_note: The rate is GIVEN and the time is asked, so set dN/dt = 300 and solve. That is the reverse of the usual direction, and reading it the other way makes the question impossible.
